reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the link between 500°C heat treatment, peak microhardness, and lowest room-temperature wear rate in CoCrFeNiMn coatings, but it does not address FeNiCrCoCu, high-temperature wear, or the formation of a protective Cr2O3 oxide film. The oxide film premise is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Heat treatment at ~500°C maximizes microhardness in HEA coatings
Peak microhardness at 500°C is due to a heterogeneous nanostructure with nanotwins and dislocations
Heat treatment above 500°C causes recrystallization, grain coarsening, and hardness decrease
